answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making every identity carry a verifiable record of work before its voice gains weight. A newcomer starts at a blank atlas: nothing is granted, so it must contribute checkable labor and gather countersignatures from established peers before its vote counts. Reputation grows like an oasis fed by real springs, and a farm of freshly minted keys brings no water with it. Because influence follows witnessed tenure rather than account count, a thousand synthetic accounts send only a faint signal that the ledger cannot mistake for honest history.
